title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
provenance: community consensus (AppleGamingWiki / r-macgaming / MacPlay), unverified by Highball Report with details from WaterWANG-1014 (highball-db#38, 2026-09-14), Apple M4 Max, macOS 15.7.7, Highball 0.9.11, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r2, DXMT, rated 3 of 5 (playable with workarounds). Not verified by the maintainer. v1kk5 (highball-db#382, 2026-10-07): rated 4 after 23 minutes, Apple M1, macOS 27.0, Highball 0.10.10, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r21, DXMT, with .NET 4.8, XACT, Controllers through SDL and core fonts installed. wimepmitt (highball-db#713, 2026-10-26), Apple M5, macOS 26.6.2, Highball 0.10.22, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r28, DXMT, msync, rated 4 of 5 after 2 minutes, minor issues not described. babaiyu (highball-db#791, 2026-10-29), Apple M4, macOS 27.2, Highball 0.10.22, engine x64-crossover26.3-r27, D3DMetal, esync, AVX advertised, frame cap 120, rated 3 of 5 after 38 minutes: the DirectX 12 build with a third-party fix (witcher3-crossover-fix, MIT, which links bin/x64 to x64_dx12 and replaces amd_fidelityfx_loader_dx12.dll with a proxy that refuses one stream-output pipeline), --launcher-skip, HDR and DLSS/Reflex off and FXAA.
notes: DirectX 11 build on DXMT is the reported way to play. Reported on an M4 Max: the CD Projekt RED launcher (REDlauncher.exe) that Steam starts first fails with "Failed to create OpenGL context for QSurfaceFormat", a Qt rendering problem in the launcher rather than the game. Workaround the reporter used, start bin/x64/witcher3.exe (the DirectX 11 build) directly, with Steam running, and the game launches on DXMT. Steam's own --launcher-skip option skips the launcher too but starts the DirectX 12 build, which needs D3DMetal, not measured here. In game the reporter sees the mouse pointer offset from where clicks and aim land, not yet resolved; running windowed at the display's own resolution is the usual remedy for that class of problem and is not verified for this game. No measurement by the maintainer yet. A second report, on an M1, rates it 4 after 23 minutes on DXMT and names no problem. A third report plays the DirectX 12 build on D3DMetal on the Wine 11 engine r27 with a player-made fix (see the known issues).

knownIssues.symptom: The CD Projekt RED launcher fails before the game with "Failed to create OpenGL context for QSurfaceFormat" (reported on an M4 Max, DXMT)
knownIssues.cause: reported, the launcher is a Qt app drawing through OpenGL and that path is not available under this Wine
knownIssues.fix: start bin/x64/witcher3.exe (the DirectX 11 build) directly with Steam running, for example by dropping it onto Highball, which runs it in the environment; --launcher-skip as a Steam launch option also skips it but picks the DirectX 12 build

knownIssues.symptom: Mouse pointer drawn away from where clicks and aim land in game (reported)
knownIssues.fix: none verified, try windowed mode at the display's own resolution

knownIssues.symptom: The DirectX 12 build (patch 5.00b) shows a black screen on D3DMetal
knownIssues.cause: per the README of a player-made fix: D3DMetal crashes on one stream-output pipeline and the game's crash handler then deadlocks. Not measured here. The fix's other part, a bin/x64 link, answers a redirect CrossOver's app makes, which Highball's engines don't (checked in CrossOver 26.3's Wine source)
knownIssues.fix: the DirectX 11 build on DXMT (above), or the player-made witcher3-crossover-fix with --launcher-skip, HDR and DLSS/Reflex off and FXAA (highball-db#791). It replaces a game DLL with a proxy and has not been reviewed by Highball
